vignette: Meet Raymond, a 61-year-old married bus driver who has been struggling to shake off the memories of his torture experience. It's been years since the incident, but for Raymond, the terror lingers, especially at night. He finds it harder to feel safe in the darkness, and his mind becomes increasingly vigilant, listening for any sound that might indicate someone is entering his home. This heightened sense of threat has become a self-reinforcing cycle, where his own fears fuel his perception of danger. Raymond's memories of the event are fragmented, with some moments etched vividly in his mind while others remain shrouded in darkness. Remembering the event brings back the same terror he felt at the time, and he often finds himself wondering what really happened during those lost hours. This incomplete picture haunts him, leaving him with more questions than answers. As he recalls the moments of clarity, he is met with an overwhelming sense of guilt - a feeling that has become his constant companion. For Raymond, the guilt stems from his perceived inaction during the torture. He believes he should have done more to stop what happened, and this self-blame has led him to view himself as weak. This negative appraisal of himself has become a lens through which he views the world, influencing how he perceives threats around him. His fear of being vulnerable again drives his hypervigilance at night, making it difficult for him to shake off the feeling that danger is lurking in every shadow. As Raymond navigates his daily routine as a bus driver, these fears and memories continue to simmer just below the surface. The sound of screeching brakes or the sight of a familiar landmark can trigger a cascade of physical reactions - a racing heart, sweating palms, and an overwhelming sense of dread. These reminders serve as a painful link between his past trauma and present-day reality. The weight of these memories and fears has taken a toll on Raymond's relationships and daily life. He has become increasingly withdrawn, avoiding social interactions that might trigger more memories or feelings of vulnerability. His wife, once a source of comfort, now feels helpless in the face of his anguish. As Raymond struggles to break free from this cycle of fear and guilt, he is met with the daunting realization that he may never be able to forgive himself for what happened. Despite the darkness that surrounds him, Raymond has finally mustered the courage to seek help. He hopes that therapy will provide a safe space to confront his memories, reframe his negative appraisals, and learn to live with the terror of his past without being consumed by it. As he begins this journey, he is most afraid of confronting the aspects of himself that he has tried to keep hidden - the weakness, the guilt, and the shame. Yet, deep down, Raymond yearns for a chance to rediscover himself, to find a way to heal and move forward, free from the shackles of his traumatic past.
